diagrams.prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational / style-transfer.
Asset type: full-color handbook diagram, candidate 1, landscape 3:2, high-resolution.
Primary request: Redraw "Port and Starboard tacks" as a refined color windsurfing illustration matching the supplied dock illustration.
INPUT ROLES: Image 1 (dock) is the authoritative style reference: painterly teal water, feathered white edge, crisp navy outlines, soft dimensional shadows, cream labels with restrained orange accents, dark navy serif headings. Image 2 (source PDF page) shows the old tacks diagram; use only its top diagram and instructional concept, not its surrounding prose or other diagrams.
COMPOSITION: Large title "Port and starboard tacks" above two equally sized illustrated water panels. Left panel titled "PORT TACK", right panel "STARBOARD TACK". At the top of BOTH panels, three navy wind arrows point straight DOWN, explicitly labeled "Wind". Maintain the SAME wind direction in both panels.
Each panel shows THREE distinct, clearly recognizable WINDSURF boards, not dinghies, viewed directly from above, spaced vertically with small navy direction arrows continuing straight ahead of each pointed bow. Bow/nose visibly pointed and tail squared; all boards have an attached mast/boom/sail, no people. Slim blue-and-white boards, lime-and-white translucent sails with navy spars; tasteful orange details. Their physical orientation and arrows must agree.
LEFT / PORT panel: top board bow points diagonally UPPER RIGHT (northeast, 45 degrees); middle board bow points RIGHT (east); bottom board bow points LOWER RIGHT (southeast, 135 degrees from the incoming wind). In all three, the wind comes from the board's LEFT side when facing its bow. Sails lie to leeward, generally toward the lower side of the picture, never upwind. Label each board with a small readable "P".
RIGHT / STARBOARD panel: mirrored headings: top board bow points UPPER LEFT (northwest); middle board bow points LEFT (west); bottom board bow points LOWER LEFT (southwest). In all three, the wind comes from the board's RIGHT side when facing its bow. Sails lie to leeward, generally toward lower side of picture. Label each board with "S".
Below the left panel write exactly: "Wind from your left." Below right panel: "Wind from your right." Single small footer line: "Left and right are relative to the direction you are sailing."
Make labels and arrows large enough to read on a phone when the image is opened full size. Use generous whitespace and a coherent quiet instructional style. No compass letters N/E/S/W, no dock or shore, no unnecessary boats, no logos/watermarks, no photorealism. Do not turn this into a website screenshot. Technical accuracy of board headings and wind directions is paramount.

diagrams.prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational / style-transfer.
Asset type: full-color handbook right-of-way decision diagram, candidate 1, portrait approximately 4:5, high-resolution.
Primary request: Redraw the old "Right-of-Way Flow Chart" from source image 2 in the same illustrated color style as the dock in image 1.
INPUT ROLES: Image 1 is the style reference, painterly teal maritime water with feathered white edges, navy serif lettering, cream rounded callout boxes edged in orange, subtle shadows and crisp navy arrows. Image 2 is the source PDF page; use ONLY the middle decision flowchart as the layout/content reference. Do not copy the old surrounding text about towing.
COMPOSITION: An elegant portrait infographic, white outer margins, a very faint teal water wash inside, enough contrast for easy reading. Large dark navy serif title exactly "Right-of-way rules". Subtitle exactly "Between two sailing vessels".
Three sequential numbered cream decision cards stacked DOWN THE LEFT/CENTER. Outcomes in equally legible orange-bordered cream cards to the RIGHT. Clear navy connecting lines, no overlaps, no ambiguity, no tiny text. Use YES branches to the right, NO branches down. Keep typography large, short lines, generous padding. Decision order is essential: overtaking is checked FIRST.
Exact flow:
Decision 1: "Is one vessel overtaking the other?"
Right arrow labeled "Yes" to outcome: "The overtaking vessel keeps clear."
Down arrow labeled "No" to decision 2.
Decision 2: "Are they on opposite tacks?"
Right arrow labeled "Yes" to outcome: "Port tack keeps clear of starboard tack."
Down arrow labeled "No" to decision 3.
Decision 3: "They are on the same tack."
Right arrow (without Yes/No label) to outcome: "Windward keeps clear of leeward."
Keep outcome cards visually connected ONLY to the correct question. The third card is a statement, not a question.
Two clear footer strips across the full width:
"Give way: act early and keep well clear."
"Stand on: keep course and speed; act if needed to avoid collision."
No towing rule. No claim this is a complete rule set for all vessel types. No green/red traffic lights. No decorative vessels or people that clutter the flowchart. Match dock artwork's warm cream, navy, orange, turquoise and soft paper texture. This is an instructional diagram, not a webpage, poster advertisement or photorealistic scene. Spell all words exactly.

Preserve every decision box, outcome box, connector, arrow, Yes/No label, number, exact wording, typography, relative position, title, subtitle, footer strips, proportions and navy/cream/orange/teal color palette. Do not change the diagram's flow or add anything. Keep the three numbered cards and all arrows completely intact. The result should be a polished clean flowchart matching the dock illustration's maritime style.

diagrams.prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational / style-transfer.
Asset type: full-color windsurfing handbook diagram, candidate 1, square, high-resolution.
Primary request: Redraw "Points of sail" from the bottom diagram in source image 2, matching the color illustration style of image 1.
INPUT ROLES: Image 1 (dock) provides style: painterly turquoise/teal water, feathered white edges, navy outlines and dark navy serif lettering, quiet soft shadows, cream labels and orange highlights. Image 2 provides ONLY the old circular points-of-sail diagram, not the surrounding page, tacks diagram or flowchart.
COMPOSITION AND EXACT GEOMETRY:
Title "Points of sail" across the top. A large, clean circular teaching diagram on very pale teal water. Three parallel navy arrows at the top labeled "Wind" point vertically DOWN. The wind comes FROM the TOP of the page throughout.
A small center dot represents the common reference position. Thin dashed radial guide lines. A softly orange-shaded NO-SAIL wedge extends UP from the center, bounded by rays at 45 degrees left and 45 degrees right of straight up (a 90-degree wedge overall). Label "No-sail zone" in its upper center; smaller "About 45° either side of the wind". No board inside this wedge.
Show SEVEN recognizable slim WINDSURF boards with mast/boom/sail, seen from directly above and placed around the circle, never dinghies or yachts. Each board's pointed NOSE faces AWAY FROM THE CENTER along its radial heading. Direction arrows point the SAME way as each board's nose. Blue-and-white board decks with squared tails, navy outlines, lime-and-white sails positioned to leeward. No people. Bow vs tail and heading must be unambiguous.
1 Upper-left board at northwest: bow points NORTHWEST / upper-left. Label "Close-hauled" and "≈45°".
2 Upper-right board at northeast: bow points NORTHEAST / upper-right. Label "Close-hauled" and "≈45°".
3 Far-left board at west: bow points LEFT, exactly horizontal. Label "Beam reach" and "90°".
4 Far-right board at east: bow points RIGHT, exactly horizontal. Label "Beam reach" and "90°".
5 Lower-left board at southwest: bow points LOWER LEFT. Label "Broad reach" and "≈135°".
6 Lower-right board at southeast: bow points LOWER RIGHT. Label "Broad reach" and "≈135°".
7 Bottom board at south: bow points straight DOWN. Label "Run" and "180°".
Labels arranged with generous space beside their corresponding boards, no overlaps or crossed leader lines, no text on sails. At beam reach the sail opens to leeward (toward bottom of picture). At run the sail is eased out broadly to the side. Retain painterly water but keep it sufficiently light for navy text to be readable. Use a quiet white/cream outer background and orange accent only for no-sail wedge and small details.
Footer: "Angles are measured from the direction the wind comes from."
No compass letters or north arrow: these are wind-relative directions, not geographic directions. No claim of fixed performance for every board, no detailed angle bands, no extra boards, no logos or watermarks. Prioritize accurate geometry, clear readable labels and consistency with the dock illustration.
